deliverables: Maintenance of the existing Scalus stack and supported export targets
Dijkstra hard-fork readiness across smart contracts, transaction building, emulation, and testing
Improved interoperability with existing Cardano tooling and the broader JVM ecosystem
A first scoped application runtime validated through reference applications, integration tests, and early-user feedback
Three quarterly milestones from July 2026 to March 2027
request.what: Funding for a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by projects including Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
Scalus components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js reaches more than 20,000 downloads per month.
The proposal reduces the prior Scalus request from ₳8,503,000 over 12 months to approximately ₳2,464,844 over 9 months with no contingency.
The funded scope excludes a standalone L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Delivery is milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
Lantr Engineering states that every prior Scalus milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery.
The proposed runtime would support chain data following, on-chain event reactions, time-based scheduling, backend workflow coordination, and failure recovery.
The proposal frames Scalus as shared open-source Cardano infrastructure under the Apache 2.0 license that can benefit multiple teams, tools, and products.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus over 9 months, focused on maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime, while presenting prior adoption, reduced scope, and milestone-based governance as key support.
